readings: For patients who have at least one single lab record in which `U-PRO` = '-' and `RA` = '-' (both in the same record), list each patient's ID, their sex (from the Patient table, only patients present there), and the average `ALP` and average `HCT` across ALL of that patient's lab records, not only the qualifying ones. Ignore missing values and do not round. Group by patient ID and sex, sort by average `HCT` from highest to lowest with missing averages last, and show the top 10.

For patients who have at least one lab record with `U-PRO` = '-' and at least one lab record with `RA` = '-', where the two records may be different records or the same one, list each patient's ID, their sex (from the Patient table, only patients present there), and the average `ALP` and average `HCT` across ALL of that patient's lab records. Ignore missing values and do not round. Group by patient ID and sex, sort by average `HCT` from highest to lowest with missing averages last, and show the top 10.
queries:
SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALP) AS avg_ALP, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_HCT
FROM Patient p
JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID
WHERE p.ID IN (
    SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-'
)
GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
ORDER BY avg_HCT IS NULL, avg_HCT DESC
LIMIT 10;
SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALP) AS avg_ALP, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_HCT
FROM Patient p
JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID
WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-')
  AND p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE RA = '-')
GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
ORDER BY avg_HCT IS NULL, avg_HCT DESC
LIMIT 10;
